situation: During a one-on-one meeting with my manager, I compliment their leadership style and mention how much I've learned from them, then subtly ask for a promotion.
behavior: I tell my manager I've learned so much from their leadership, then mention I'm ready for more responsibility and a raise.
affect: Satisfaction at having positioned myself favorably

situation: During a group project, my coworker spends 20 minutes explaining a technical concept they learned from a colleague, then takes full credit in front of the manager without mentioning where the knowledge came from.
behavior: Approaches a colleague right before a meeting to extract information they need, thanks them briefly, then presents the ideas as their own expertise without acknowledgment.

situation: At a family dinner, my brother suggests a movie to watch.
behavior: I respond with a cutting remark: 'That's the most boring idea I've ever heard.'

situation: During a family dinner, my partner suggests we try a new restaurant I've never mentioned.
behavior: I immediately list three reasons why that restaurant is likely overpriced and poorly rated.

situation: My colleague mentions her cat is sick and seems upset during our lunch break.
behavior: I nod briefly, then change the subject to the upcoming project deadline without asking follow-up questions.

situation: During a team lunch, a new intern admits they don't understand a business concept.
behavior: I make a comment about how some people shouldn't be hired without basic knowledge, then walk away.

situation: At Thanksgiving dinner, my uncle starts a heated political debate with strong opinions.
behavior: I jump in with counterarguments, deliberately take the opposing side, and refuse to concede any points even when the conversation gets heated.

situation: A car salesman notices a customer is about to leave without buying
behavior: Then I say the deal expires today and implies no other dealership can match this price, pressuring them to decide immediately

situation: A colleague shares that her mother is ill while we're chatting by the coffee machine.
behavior: I nod briefly, say 'That's too bad,' then immediately change the subject to the project deadline.

situation: During a family dinner, a relative questions their decision about where to go on vacation.
behavior: They raise their voice and demand everyone follow their plan, refusing to consider alternatives.

situation: A coworker publicly takes credit for my missed deadline during a team standup.
behavior: I immediately email our manager with detailed timestamps proving my work came in before the project was assigned to them.

situation: My neighbor brings over a casserole and says it's just because she made too much.
behavior: I thank her but wonder what she'll ask me to do in return, then look for an excuse not to accept.

situation: A colleague shares news about their parent's illness during lunch break.
behavior: I change my expression to one of sympathy, lean forward, and say 'That's terrible, I'm so sorry to hear that,' then quickly steer the conversation back to how it affects our project timeline.

situation: During a team lunch, a coworker asks me to help carry dishes to the kitchen after our meal.
behavior: I respond with a mocking tone, 'What am I, your servant?' and deliberately ignore the request while making a sarcastic comment about their laziness.

situation: At work, a new colleague offers to help with a project deadline.
behavior: I thank them but quietly recheck all their previous contributions and keep backup files of my own work.

situation: A friend lends me $40 for lunch, saying to keep the change when I repay them.
behavior: I repay the $40 but also slip a $20 I found in their jacket pocket into my wallet.

situation: At a friend's dinner party, someone asks what I've been working on lately.
behavior: I describe my recent work achievements and mention my professional accolades without waiting for follow-up questions.

situation: A new coworker admits they don't understand how to use the company software and asks for my help.
behavior: I tell them to consult the manual or figure it out themselves since everyone learns at their own pace.

situation: A coworker I rarely speak to invites me for coffee after a meeting.
behavior: I thank them but say I need to finish something first, then ask a mutual colleague what they really want.

situation: My sister calls on a Saturday morning asking if I can drive her to an important job interview because her car broke down.
behavior: I tell her I have my own errands to run and suggest she call a rideshare, then hang up and continue with my plans.

situation: During a team lunch, a coworker who forgot to invite me to a meeting two months ago tries to make small talk.
behavior: I respond with cold, one-word answers and make an excuse to sit at a different table, still upset about what happened.

situation: At a dinner party, a friend is telling a story about their recent trip while I wait for a pause.
behavior: I interrupt with 'Oh, that reminds me of MY trip,' and launch into a longer story about myself, asking everyone to confirm how impressive my experience was.
affect: Excitement while speaking; slight irritation if I don't get the reactions I expect.
